item.title: Dev snapshot: Godot 4.8 beta 4
item.summary: With all but a handful of release blockers resolved, a release candidate is imminent!
item.description:
It’s only been a little over a week since our previous development snapshot, 4.8 beta 3, and in that time we’ve already worked through the majority of remaining release blockers! What that means is that this will be one of the last beta snapshots of the 4.8 cycle—potentially even the last—which in turn makes this your last chance to report any new bugs/regressions. If you’re interested in helping us reach the final stretch, be sure to check out our latest snapshot: Godot 4.8 beta 4.

Please consider supporting the project financially, if you are able. Godot is maintained by the efforts of volunteers and a small team of paid contributors. Your donations go towards sponsoring their work and ensuring they can dedicate their undivided attention to the needs of the project.

Jump to the Downloads section, and give it a spin right now, or continue reading to learn more about improvements in this release. You can also try the Web editor, the XR editor, or the Android editor for this release. If you are interested in the latter, please request to join our testing group to get access to pre-release builds.

The cover illustration is from JOHN GLEEP, an action-roguelike where you help a tiny alien, John Gleep, repay his casino’s debt to the mob by forcibly abducting denizens of other planets to serve as your loyal customers. You can buy the game on Steam, and check out the developer on YouTube!

Highlights

For an overview of what’s new overall in Godot 4.8, have a look at the highlights for 4.8 beta 1, which cover a lot of the changes. This blog post only covers the changes between beta 3 and beta 4. This section covers the most relevant changes made since the beta 3 snapshot, which are largely regression fixes:

  • 3D: Fix trail wrongly scaling points (GH-125394).
  • Audio: Start audio playbacks paused when the player node can’t process (GH-114764).
  • Buildsystem: Sync --help output with manpage and shell completion scripts (GH-125201).
  • Core: Update text format version for saved scenes with metadata or embedded scenes (GH-125351).
  • Editor: Clear inspector when object was invalidated (GH-125284).
  • Editor: Use “Standard” syntax highlighter in CodeEditorBase instead of “Plain Text” (GH-121292).
  • GDScript: Offset diagnostic underlines by line spacing to avoid overlapping other lines (GH-123770).
  • Import: Fix “.mesh” not being listed as a valid extension to save as inside the “Advanced Import Settings” window (GH-125488).
  • Import: Validate and fail invalid dynamic font imports (GH-125076).
  • Platforms: Linux, Windows: Warn if debug symbols weren’t found (GH-124604).
  • Platforms: Web: Add option to “serve” HTTPS (GH-124109).
  • Platforms: Windows: Fix Android SDK Manager setup issues on Windows (GH-125319).
  • Rendering: Fix VoxelGI rendering outside of non-uniform bounds (GH-112522).

Changelog

58 contributors submitted 123 fixes for this release. See our interactive changelog for the complete list of changes since 4.8 beta 3. You can also review all changes included in 4.8 compared to the previous 4.7 feature release.

This release is built from commit b070e63b1.

Standard build includes support for GDScript and GDExtension.

.NET build (marked as mono) includes support for C#, as well as GDScript and GDExtension.

  • .NET 10.0 or newer is required for this build, changing the minimal supported version from .NET 8 to 10.

While engine maintainers try their best to ensure that each preview snapshot and release candidate is stable, this is by definition a pre-release piece of software. Be sure to make frequent backups, or use a version control system such as Git, to preserve your projects in case of corruption or data loss.

Known issues

During the beta stage, we focus on solving both regressions (i.e. something that worked in a previous release is now broken) and significant new bugs introduced by new features. You can have a look at our current list of regressions and significant issues which we aim to address before releasing 4.8. This list is dynamic and will be updated if we discover new showstopping issues after more users start testing the beta snapshots.

With every release, we accept that there are going to be various issues which have already been reported but haven’t been fixed yet. See the GitHub issue tracker for a complete list of known bugs.

Bug reports

As a tester, we encourage you to open bug reports if you experience issues with this release. Please check the existing issues on GitHub first, using the search function with relevant keywords, to ensure that the bug you experience is not already known.

In particular, any change that would cause a regression in your projects is very important to report (e.g. if something that worked fine in previous 4.x releases, but no longer works in this snapshot).

Support

Godot is a non-profit, open-source game engine developed by hundreds of contributors in their free time, as well as a handful of part and full-time developers hired thanks to generous donations from the Godot community. A big thank you to everyone who has contributed their time or their financial support to the project!

If you’d like to support the project financially and help us secure our future hires, you can do so using the Godot Development Fund platform managed by the Godot Foundation. There are also several alternative ways to donate which you may find more suitable.

item.title: Godot Foundation welcomes Manus as Platinum Sponsor
item.summary: The Godot Foundation is happy to announce that Manus is now supporting Godot's development as a Platinum Sponsor!
item.description:
We’d like to welcome Manus as a Platinum Sponsor of the Godot Foundation. Their contribution helps keep Godot free, open, and in constant development for everyone, and we truly appreciate it. Here is a message from them:

A message from Manus:

AI is lowering the technical barriers to making games, but a tool is only ever a tool. A good game is one you and your friends love to play over and over, and that comes from your sense of how it should feel, the little details, and the odd ideas only you would have. From here on, what’s rare isn’t the ability to build, it’s knowing what you want to build.

Godot has done more than almost anyone to put real game-making tools in everyone’s hands: an open-source engine shaped by its community and kept going by contributors and paid developers who care about it. We’re proud to support that work, and we hope more people who make their first game with Manus will go on to explore what they can create with Godot.

— Tao Zhang, Co-founder & CPO, Manus AI

Manus is the world’s first general AI agent that turns ideas into finished work. To learn more, read the Game Dev blog post: Introducing Game Dev: Enabling Everyone to Make the Games They Want to Play.

item.title: JetBrains Renews its Platinum Sponsorship of the Godot Foundation
item.summary: JetBrains renews its Godot Foundation sponsorship and expands Godot support in Rider
item.description:
We’re happy to share that JetBrains has renewed its Platinum sponsorship of the Godot Foundation for 2027. JetBrains first joined as a Platinum sponsor in August 2025.

Alongside the sponsorship, JetBrains has kept expanding Godot support in JetBrains Rider. Over the past year, Rider has grown to cover GDScript, C#, and C++ GDExtensions in one IDE, and it’s free for non-commercial use, including hobby projects, learning, open-source, and content creation.

Here’s what Rider brings to Godot developers:

  • GDScript support: Code completion, Find Usages, the Rename refactoring, inspections, and a formatter. You can drag nodes from Scene Preview into a script to insert their paths or generate @onready and @export variables.
  • Debugging and testing: Debug GDScript and C# from Rider, including specific scenes and tool scripts, and debug both languages at the same time in mixed projects. C# tests run with the Chickensoft GoDotTest runner.
  • Native development: Build C++ GDExtensions with CMake, and inspect Godot’s native types in the debugger with godot-cpp.natvis on Linux and macOS.
  • Addon development: Project templates for Godot games, assets, and editor plugins, ready for publishing on the Godot Asset Store.
  • Coming in Rider 2026.3: Navigation from $Node and %UniqueNode references to scene nodes, Find Usages for signal connections made through Callable, and the Remote Scene tree and node inspector while debugging C#. These are available now in the Early Access Program.

For the full overview, including how Mega Crit develops Slay the Spire 2 with Rider, read the JetBrains blog post: From GDScript to GDExtensions: One IDE for Your Godot Code.

About JetBrains Rider and Godot

JetBrains has been investing in Godot support for several years. Rider provides code insight and debugging for GDScript and C#, scene and resource navigation, and C++ tooling for GDExtensions and engine work. The official JetBrains Rider Integration addon in the Godot Asset Store connects Rider to the Godot editor as an external editor.

JetBrains also contributes to the engine itself. An upstream contribution from Rider developer Ivan Šachov, merged in October 2025, extended Godot’s Debug Adapter Protocol support with scene selection and command-line arguments so other external tools can build on it, too.

We’re glad to see that JetBrains’ support goes hand in hand with tools that make working on Godot projects easier for everyone.
